findings.claim: The pooled analysis is not uniformly intention-to-treat: PMID 39529939 contributes an efficacy analysis excluding randomized participants. The summary should describe the mixed analysis populations.

findings.page_quote: endpoint 18410562 diarrhoea (>or=3 loose or watery stools/day for >or=48 h occurring during or up to 2 weeks after the antibiotic therapy)

source_evidence.quote: Three (2.5%) children in the probiotic group developed AAD (diarrhoea caused by Clostridium difficile or otherwise unexplained diarrhoea) compared to nine (7.5%) in the placebo group (RR 0.33, 95% CI 0.1-1.06).

findings.claim: The compatibility table assigns the any-diarrhoea definition to the narrower AAD result actually pooled. The extracted RR is correct, but its endpoint description omits the etiological restriction.

source_evidence.quote: The primary outcome was the proportion of patients who developed diarrhea in the first 21 days after enrollment.

findings.claim: The page mistakes the 14-day intervention duration for the outcome observation window, which was 21 days.

findings.page_quote: 12 missed trial(s) have no own-publication registry linkage — unregistered / pre-registration-era, so unreachable by any registry-first search

source_evidence.quote: This trial is registered, number ISRCTN70017204.

findings.claim: The explanation incorrectly characterizes all listed misses as unregistered or lacking publication-to-registry linkage. Listed PMID 23932219 explicitly supplies its registration; failure of the particular retrieval route does not establish unreachability by any registry-first search.

findings.page_quote: an effect from a risk-factor / multivariable model is not the randomised contrast.

source_evidence.quote: Using a multivariate model to adjust for two independent risk factors for AAD (age and days of cephalosporin use), the adjusted relative risk was significantly protective for S. boulardii (RR = 0.29, 95% CI = 0.08, 0.98).

findings.claim: The source identifies 0.29 as the adjusted treatment effect for S. boulardii, not an effect of a separate risk factor. Selecting the crude RR can be a methodological choice, but the notice's stated justification misrepresents the reported estimate.

source_evidence.quote: S. boulardii also reduced the risk of antibiotic-associated diarrhoea (diarrhoea caused by Clostridium difficile or otherwise unexplained diarrhoea) compared with placebo [four of 119 (3.4%) vs. 22 of 127 (17.3%), relative risk: 0.2; 95% confidence interval: 0.07-0.5].

findings.claim: The selection label incorrectly says no target published effect exists: the abstract reports an RR and CI for these exact AAD counts. This finding concerns the selection label, not the validity of the displayed counts.
